Salutary

SAL-yuh-ter-ee · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Salutary is producing good effects; beneficial, especially in an unexpected or instructive way.

The company's near-bankruptcy proved oddly salutary, forcing managers to finally fix wasteful habits they'd ignored for years.

Worked Example

The coach called the humiliating loss a salutary experience, since it exposed exactly which plays the team needed to fix.

Salutary describes something that produces a genuinely good result, even if the experience itself was unpleasant.

How Salutary Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

beneficial

beneficial: producing good results

wholesome

wholesome: good for physical or moral well-being

Antonyms

harmful

harmful: causing damage or injury

damaging

damaging: causing harm

How Strong Is It? — helpful → salutary → transformative

helpful vs. salutary

helpful vs. salutary: Helpful means useful or beneficial in a mild, ordinary way, less striking than salutary.

transformative vs. salutary

transformative vs. salutary: Transformative means producing dramatic, life-changing benefit, an even stronger positive effect than salutary.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — salut-

root — salut-: health, safety, well-being (from Latin salus, salutis)

suffix — -ary

suffix — -ary: relating to (Latin -arius)

Put it together

Put it together: Salutary is built from salut- ('health, safety, well-being,' from Latin salus, salutis) + -ary ('relating to') -- literally 'relating to health or well-being.'

Use the root in a new word: salutation

Use the root in a new word: salutation: The letter opened with a formal salutation: 'Dear Sir or Madam.'
